status_why: Massachusetts publishes no statewide count on the night; cities and towns post their own, and the state posts certified results weeks later.
office: the Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth
system: No statewide live results. Cities and towns post their own unofficial results on the night (Boston: boston.gov); the Secretary's PD43+ (ElectionStats) holds certified results only, weeks later

races_in_feed: certified: everything (statewide, Congress, legislature, Governor's Council, county offices, questions); on the night: only what each town posts
local: no county results sites; 351 cities and towns post their own (Boston, Worcester, Springfield, Cambridge largest)
how_counted: Each city and town counts and posts its own results; the state publishes totals after certification.

certify.rule: Members of Congress, state officers and legislators: not before 5 p.m. on the 15th day after the election (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 54, 116).
certify.local_rule: Cities and towns send certified copies within 15 days (ch. 54, 112).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

scout_blocked: www.sec.state.ma.us is behind Incapsula (CLAUDE.md, 2026-09-30); electionstats.state.ma.us is not
scout_plan: No live source for the whole state. The Associated Press gathers Massachusetts returns from the town clerks under a long-standing arrangement and resells them; that is not open. On the night Election Night can show Boston's own unofficial precinct results (one reader) and say plainly that Massachusetts publishes no statewide count until certification; the statewide and congressional map fills from ElectionStats when it is certified. Ask John whether to read a handful of the largest cities' pages.
